questions.question: In this experiment, the KNN classifier was trained using which dataset?

explanations.a: Incorrect because the Wine dataset is used for other classification experiments, not this simulation.
explanations.b: Correct because the Iris dataset was used to train and evaluate the KNN classifier.
explanations.c: Incorrect because MNIST is an image dataset used for digit recognition.
explanations.d: Incorrect because CIFAR-10 is an image classification dataset.

questions.question: How many features were used as input variables in the KNN model for this experiment?

explanations.a: Incorrect because the Iris dataset contains more than two attributes.
explanations.b: Incorrect because the dataset contains four measurement features.
explanations.c: Correct because the features used were sepal length, sepal width, petal length, and petal width.
explanations.d: Incorrect because the Iris dataset does not contain five features.

questions.question: In the experiment, the dataset was divided into training and testing sets using which ratio?

explanations.a: Incorrect because the dataset was not split equally.
explanations.b: Correct because 70% of the data was used for training and 30% for testing.
explanations.c: Incorrect because this split was not used in this simulation.
explanations.d: Incorrect because the testing dataset would be too small for evaluation.

questions.question: Why was StandardScaler used before training the KNN model?

answers.a: To increase the number of samples
answers.b: To normalize feature ranges for fair distance calculation

explanations.a: Incorrect because scaling does not change dataset size.
explanations.b: Correct because KNN relies on distance metrics that are affected by feature magnitude.
explanations.c: Incorrect because scaling does not handle missing data.
explanations.d: Incorrect because scaling only affects feature values.

questions.question: What does the parameter k represent in the KNN classifier used in this experiment?

answers.a: The number of clusters in the dataset
answers.b: The number of nearest neighbours considered for prediction
answers.c: The number of features used in the dataset
answers.d: The number of training samples in the dataset

explanations.a: Incorrect because clustering refers to unsupervised algorithms such as K-Means, not KNN classification.
explanations.b: Correct because k determines how many neighbouring data points participate in majority voting during classification.
explanations.c: Incorrect because features describe attributes of the data and are not controlled by the parameter k.
explanations.d: Incorrect because k only specifies how many neighbours are used for prediction, not the dataset size.

questions.question: In this experiment, the confusion matrix was used to:

answers.b: Visualize correct and incorrect predictions for each class
answers.d: Split the dataset into training and testing sets

explanations.a: Incorrect because confusion matrices do not modify model performance.
explanations.b: Correct because the confusion matrix compares predicted and actual class labels.
explanations.c: Incorrect because scaling is done using preprocessing techniques.
explanations.d: Incorrect because dataset splitting is done earlier in preprocessing.

questions.question: Which evaluation metric indicates the overall proportion of correctly classified samples?

explanations.a: Incorrect because precision measures the proportion of correct positive predictions.
explanations.b: Incorrect because recall measures the ability to detect actual positives.
explanations.c: Correct because accuracy represents the overall proportion of correct predictions.
explanations.d: Incorrect because F1-Score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.

questions.question: ROC-AUC in this experiment was computed using which strategy?

explanations.a: Correct because multi-class ROC-AUC was calculated using the One-vs-Rest approach.
explanations.b: Incorrect because regression is not used to compute ROC curves.
explanations.c: Incorrect because clustering is unrelated to ROC evaluation.
explanations.d: Incorrect because ROC-AUC does not involve gradient optimization.

questions.question: Based on the experiment results, high accuracy indicates that:

answers.a: The classifier correctly predicts most samples in the dataset

explanations.a: Correct because high accuracy means a large proportion of predictions match the true labels.
explanations.b: Incorrect because accuracy does not affect dataset size.
explanations.d: Incorrect because the model remains a supervised learning algorithm.

questions.question: Why is stratified sampling used while splitting the dataset in this experiment?

answers.a: To increase the number of samples in the dataset
answers.b: To ensure each class is proportionally represented in training and testing sets
answers.c: To reduce the number of features in the dataset

explanations.a: Incorrect because stratified sampling does not change the dataset size.
explanations.b: Correct because stratified sampling maintains the same class distribution in both subsets.
explanations.c: Incorrect because feature selection and stratified sampling are different processes.
explanations.d: Incorrect because normalization is performed during feature scaling.
